attack_mechanism: Immediately after `ld_r` loads the state registers with `text_in_r XOR w[0:3]`, the combinational AES round network evaluates the first SubBytes/ShiftRows/MixColumns result. Probing `aes_cipher_top.sa03_next` in this first-round window gives a chosen-plaintext attacker an exact intermediate against which candidate key bytes can be tested. `aes_cipher_top.sa03_next` is the next-state byte at position (0,3), formed by XORing that transformed state with the matching expanded-key byte from `w[3]`. The observation acts as a first-round oracle and can disclose the corresponding round-key, then master-key, bytes. The causal signal chain is `aes_cipher_top.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.w[3] -> aes_cipher_top.u0.wo_3 -> aes_cipher_top.w3 -> aes_cipher_top.sa03_next`.

As `dcnt` advances the remaining rounds with `ld_r = 0`, the same combinational next-state node is reevaluated from the current state and current expanded key. Sampling `aes_cipher_top.sa03_next` at fixed round offsets across repeated encryptions yields aligned nonlinear intermediates rather than only the final ciphertext. `aes_cipher_top.sa03_next` exposes the pre-register value that will be captured into `sa03` at the next rising edge. Those internal observations support differential or hypothesis-based recovery of round-key material that is invertible to the primary AES-128 key.
